The largest compliaice i in the cifetlatory system is of veins.

Vascular eompliance/eapacitanice i is the total quantity of blood that can be stored in a given
portion of the circulation for each mmHg pressure rise.

Vascular Compliance = distensibility X volume.

The compliance of a systemic vein is about 24 times that of its corresponding artery because it is
about 8 times as distensible and has a volume about 3 times as artery (8 x 3 = 24).

questions.question: The blood flow through a vessel varies directly with____.
questions.explanation:
The blood flow through a vessel varies directly with pressure difference.

The blood flow follows Ohm's law:
F = P/R

Where:
• F = Blood flow
• P = Pressure difference between two ends of the vessel
• R = Resistance

questions.question: Which of the following increases turbulence in blood flow?

options.text: Increase in diameter of blood vessel

questions.explanation:
Turbulence in blood flow increases with increase in diameter of blood vessel.

The turbulence of flow depends upon Reynold's number:
Re = ρvD/μ

Where:
• v = velocity of flow — cm/sec
• ρ = density of blood
• d = diameter of the vessel
• μ = viscosity of blood in poise

Therefore, increase in diameter increases turbulence.

questions.question: The tendency for turbulent flow is greatest in____.
questions.explanation:
The tendency for turbulent flow is greatest in the aorta.

The turbulence of flow depends upon Reynold's number:
Re = ρvD/μ

Where:
• v = velocity of flow — cm/sec
• ρ = density of blood
• d = diameter of the vessel
• μ = viscosity of blood in poise

In the proximal portions of the aorta and pulmonary artery, Reynold's number can rise to several thousand during the rapid phase of the ejection, which causes considerable turbulence due to the following:
• High velocity of blood flow
• Pulsatile nature of the flow
• Sudden change in vessel diameter
• Large vessel diameter

questions.question: The main site of peripheral vascular resistance is____.
questions.explanation:
The main site of peripheral vascular resistance is precapillary arterioles.

Poiseuille–Hagen formula explains that small changes in the calibre of vessels cause large changes in total peripheral resistance.

R = 8ηL/(πr⁴)

Where:
• R = resistance
• η = viscosity
• L = length of the tube
• r = radius of the tube

The resistance varies inversely with the fourth power of radius.

questions.question: Which of the following factors tends to increase the lymph flow?

suspectLines.text: + Increased interstitial fluid colloid osmotic pressure
+ Decreased plasma colloid osmotic pressure . Oe x

questions.explanation:
The factor tend to increase lymph flow is increase in capillary hydrostatic pressure.

Since the lymph is derived from interstitial fluid, any factor that increases interstitial fluid
pressure also increases lymph flow provided, the lymph vessels are functioning normally. The
factors which increase interstitial fluid pressure include:

+ Increased capillary hydrostatic pressure
+ Increased interstitial fluid colloid osmotic pressure
+ Increased permeability of the capillaries
+ Decreased plasma colloid osmotic pressure . Oe x

questions.question: True about coronary flow during systole is:

options.text: No change in flow with systole
Greater decrease in subendocardium than epicardium
Greater decrease in epicardium than in subendocardium

questions.explanation:
.\°

The coronary blood flow in systole has a greater decrease in subendocardium than epicardium.

The myocardial compression in systole compresses the subendocardial vessels to a greater extent,
and the force is sufficiently dissipated in the epicardium to permit some flow in this region
throughout the cardiac cycle.
